full_judgment: 32. The court should be circumspect in forming its opinion relying upon such type of skewed and vacillating witness. The rule of depending upon one witness principle can be applicable in a case where there is no possibility of the presence of other witness and the witness is trustworthy, wholly reliable and not shaken in material particulars. His testimony should not be tainted with falsehood and also free from all taint so that his testimony may be believed without suspicion. This rule depends upon the facts and circumstances of each case and the same is not applicable in this case since there are others witnesses who admittedly came to the scene on hearing cries, and those witnesses also made inconsistent statements with him. Apart from the above, the neutral witnesses who were examined by P.W. 27 had been purposely withheld by the prosecution without giving any explanation, which raised natural presumption that the story introduced by the prosecution is tainted by falsehood.
